I.businessIdea: TaskFlow is a project management SaaS for small teams that combines task tracking, time tracking, and team communication in one simple, affordable tool. We compete on simplicity and price.
I.productServiceProblem: Existing project management tools are either too simple (todo lists) or too complex (Jira). Small teams need something in between that's affordable.
I.businessModel: SaaS subscription: Free tier (3 users), Pro tier ($8/user/month), Team tier ($15/user/month). Annual billing discount 20%.
I.oneYearGoals: 1,000 free users, 100 paid users, $8K MRR, and a 4.5+ rating on G2/Capterra.
I.threeYearGoals: 10,000 users, 1,500 paid, $25K MRR, and launch an enterprise tier.
I.fiveYearGoals: 50,000 users, $100K MRR, and acquisition or Series A funding.
I.customerAcquisition: Content marketing (blog + SEO), Product Hunt launch, free tier as growth engine, and integrations with popular tools (Slack, GitHub).
I.targetMarket: Small teams (3-25 people) in tech, design, marketing, and consulting. Currently using spreadsheets or overly complex tools.
I.competition: Asana, Trello, ClickUp (too complex/expensive). Todoist, Notion (too manual). We win on simplicity + price.
I.managementTeam: Founder is a full-stack developer with 10 years experience, formerly at a YC-backed startup. Designer has 7 years in product design.
I.financialOutlook: Bootstrapped with $30K savings. Seeking $150K seed for development and marketing. Projected break-even by month 14.
I.evidenceOfTraction: 500 waitlist signups, 50 beta testers, and a working MVP with 30 weekly active users.

II.companyDescription: TaskFlow is a SaaS startup making project management simple for small teams. We believe great software should be powerful without being complicated.
II.missionStatement: To help small teams do their best work with simple, powerful, and affordable project management software.
II.coreValues: Simplicity, affordability, transparency, and customer-driven development. We ship what users ask for.
II.visionStatement: To become the default project management tool for small teams worldwide, known for simplicity and value.
II.shortTermObjectives: Launch MVP, reach 1K users, get 100 paid, achieve $8K MRR, and publish on Product Hunt.
II.longTermObjectives: 10K users, $100K MRR, enterprise tier, and acquisition or Series A.
II.milestones:
1. MVP launch (month 1)
2. Product Hunt (month 2)
3. 1K users (month 4)
4. 100 paid (month 6)
5. Break-even (month 14)
II.targetMarketSummary: Small teams (3-25 people) in tech, design, marketing, and consulting who want simple, affordable project management.
II.industryContext: The project management software market is $5B and growing 10% annually. Small team segment is underserved by enterprise tools.
II.competitiveLandscape: Asana/Trello/ClickUp dominate but are increasingly complex and expensive. We compete on simplicity and price.
II.businessStructure: C-Corp — for future fundraising and equity distribution. Delaware incorporation.
II.ownershipInfo: Founder 80%, designer 10%, 10% reserved for future hires/investors.

III.productDescription: Web app with: task boards, time tracking, team chat, file sharing, calendar view, reporting, and integrations (Slack, GitHub, Google Workspace). Mobile-responsive web app.
III.keySuppliers: AWS (hosting), Stripe (payments), SendGrid (email), and GitHub (code hosting).
III.problemSolved: Small teams juggle multiple tools — tasks in Trello, time in a spreadsheet, chat in Slack. TaskFlow combines them in one simple tool at a fraction of the cost.
III.solution: All-in-one project management with a clean, intuitive interface. Free for 3 users, $8-15/user/month for larger teams.
III.keyBenefits: Simple UI, all-in-one (tasks + time + chat), affordable pricing, generous free tier, and real-time collaboration.
III.competitiveAdvantage: Simplicity — onboarding in 5 minutes, not 5 days. Price — 50% cheaper than Asana/ClickUp. Free tier drives organic growth.
III.proprietaryFeatures: Proprietary task automation engine, keyboard-first navigation, and a unique 'Focus Mode' that hides everything except your current task.
III.pricingStrategy: Free: 3 users, basic features. Pro: $8/user/month, all features. Team: $15/user/month, advanced reporting + admin. Enterprise: custom.
III.positioningRationale: We're the 'Basecamp for modern teams' — simple, opinionated, affordable. Not a swiss-army knife.
III.marginRationale: SaaS margins: hosting $0.50/user/month, support $1/user/month at scale. Gross margin 90%+. Break-even at ~200 paid users.
III.limitationsLiabilities: Single founder dependency, no mobile app yet, limited integrations, and competition from well-funded incumbents.
III.productionDelivery: Web app hosted on AWS. Responsive design works on mobile browsers. API for custom integrations.
III.intellectualProperty: Proprietary source code (closed source). Trademark for product name. Patent-pending on the Focus Mode interaction.
III.comprehensiveDescription: A SaaS project management web app combining tasks, time tracking, and team chat with a clean, intuitive interface and affordable pricing for small teams.

IV.industryOverview: The project management software market is $5B globally, growing 10% annually. The small team segment (<25 users) is the fastest-growing at 15%.
IV.industryTrends: Consolidation of tools (all-in-one platforms), AI-assisted features, mobile-first design, and freemium pricing models.
IV.targetMarketSize: 30M small teams globally using project management tools. 5M in North America. Average spend $10-20/user/month.
IV.marketShareEstimate: 0.03% of the NA market = 1,500 teams = ~15,000 users = $25K MRR by year 3.
IV.customerNeeds: Simple setup, intuitive interface, affordable pricing, essential features without bloat, and good customer support.
IV.primaryResearch: Surveyed 200 small team leads: 65% find Asana too complex, 70% want a free tier, 80% would switch for a simpler tool at lower cost.
IV.secondaryResearch: Gartner reports SMB software spending growing 12% annually. Capterra data shows 'ease of use' is the #1 buying criterion for small teams.
IV.barriersToEntry: Building a competitive product, acquiring users organically, competing with funded incumbents, and maintaining uptime/reliability.
IV.barrierStrategies: Lean MVP approach, free tier for organic growth, content marketing for SEO, and focusing on a niche (small teams) that incumbents underserve.
IV.swotStrengths: Founder's 10-year dev experience, simple product, low overhead, fast iteration.
IV.swotWeaknesses: Single founder, no sales team, limited capital, no mobile app yet.
IV.swotOpportunities: Growing SMB market, freemium model, AI features, potential acquisition target, enterprise upsell.
IV.swotThreats: Well-funded competitors (Asana raised $200M+), feature parity race, platform risk (AWS), economic downturn.
IV.swotActionPlan: Differentiate on simplicity, not features. Use free tier as growth engine. Build integrations to increase switching costs. Ship AI features.
IV.swotImmediateGoals: Launch MVP, get 1K free users, convert 100 to paid, launch on Product Hunt.
IV.swotLongTermGoals: 10K users, $100K MRR, enterprise tier, Series A or acquisition.
IV.regulatoryChanges: Data privacy regulations (GDPR, CCPA) require compliance but also create moats for compliant tools.
IV.technologyShifts: AI is transforming project management — auto-scheduling, smart priorities, natural language input. Mobile-first is now expected.
IV.economicConditions: SaaS is relatively recession-resilient. Teams still need tools, and our low price helps in a downturn.
IV.industryEvolution: Consolidation: large tools add more features, small tools get acquired. AI is the next differentiator. Open source alternatives are emerging.

V.productionProcess: Two-week sprint cycles: plan → develop → test → deploy. CI/CD pipeline. Weekly user feedback sessions. Monthly release notes.
V.productionMethods: React frontend, Node.js backend, PostgreSQL database, AWS infrastructure. Monorepo with TypeScript. Automated testing.
V.unitEconomics: Hosting: $0.50/user/month. Stripe fees: 2.9% + $0.30/transaction. Support: $1/user/month at scale. CAC: $15 (content + referrals). LTV: $240.
V.qualityControl: Automated test suite (unit + integration), staging environment, canary deployments, error monitoring (Sentry), and user feedback tracking.
V.commercialAccessibility: N/A — remote. Co-working for occasional in-person meetings.
V.commercialCosts: AWS: $500/month at launch, scaling with users. Co-working: $200/month (as needed).
V.legalLicensesPermits: Business license (Delaware C-Corp). No special permits required for SaaS.
V.legalIP: Source code (trade secret, closed source). Trademark for product name. Patent pending on Focus Mode.
V.legalRegulations: GDPR, CCPA, data breach notification laws, SOC 2 compliance (planned for enterprise tier).
